item.title: Comparison across species
item.description:
This page lines up only a summary from the “Breeding records compared” section of each species page. Please check the detailed records and sources on each species page.

  • Number ranges are built only from that species’ own records where the numbers are known. Numbers marked (needs checking) or (unverified) are not included in the ranges.
  • Records from related species and values derived from the author’s inference are not included in the ranges; only their count is shown.
  • A ［number］ is the reference number in the reference list of that species’ page.

item.title: Corydoras "Zebrina" (CW111)
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

Corydoras “Zebrina” is a fish that sells for tens of thousands of yen a pair, and wild fish can go for more than 100,000 yen. Yet little information is available in Japanese, and some shop descriptions come with a caveat that its breeding method “is presumed to be similar to other common Corydoras” (translated) (product page of a Japanese shop［28］; checked November 16, 2026).

item.title: Glossary
item.description:
Terms that appear on the species pages, listed in Japanese syllabary (gojūon) order of their Japanese readings.

F1, F2

Names for generations born in captivity. The offspring of two wild-caught parents (wild fish) are F1; the offspring of two F1 fish are F2.

Data from a related species

Numbers or observations recorded not for the species itself but for a closely related fish. On this site, the text says “data from a related species” to keep these separate from records of the species itself.
